gaps.quote: where $j\geq 0$ is the number of places its degree exceeds $r-1$
gaps.note: A term of degree r+j exceeds r-1 by j+1 places, not j places, so this definition of j is inconsistent with the degree r+j. The correct statement is that j = (degree) - r, i.e. the degree exceeds r by j (equivalently exceeds r-1 by j+1). The rule y^{r+j} = -y^j itself is correct (paper line 2778 gives the ring; the reduction follows from y^r = -1).
